questions.stem: A 32-year-old woman was readmitted to the hospital 3 days after having had a spontaneous abortion at 18 weeks gestation. On examination, she had a temperature of 38.1°C, pulse 132 beats/minute, blood pressure 85/60 mmHg, diffuse abdominal tenderness to palpation, and significant abdominal and lower extremity swelling. Blood cultures were obtained, and she was started on antibiotics. Within a few hours, her blood cultures were growing grampositive rods.
questions.lead_in: What is the most likely organism?
questions.explanation: Clostridium sordellii Clostridium sordellii infections can develop following childbirth or after gynecologic procedures and can also be seen with contaminated lacerations or in intravenous drug users. Patients may not present with high fevers but may have significant leukemoid reaction and hemoconcentration, as well as edema on examination.
questions.source: Comprehensive Review of ID · Quiz 9 Q32

questions.question: A woman has a history of intermittent bloody diarrhea for the last month. She comes in with hypotension and new hemorrhagic bullae to her lower extremities. A sample is taken, with the gram stain appearing as follows (photo of Gram Positive rods with subterminal spores, no other cells visible on stain):

parts.text: a) What are two characteristics features on Gram stain?
b) What organism is this?
c) What is one risk factor for this condition?
d) What is the recommended antimicrobial treatment?
e) What are two other interventions you might consider?

cohort_answer.text: Gram stain: Gram positive bacilli, subterminal spores. Organism: Clostridium septicum (if no trauma; C. perfringens if trauma). Risk factor: spontaneous gas gangrene with diarrhea history suggests GI entry, possible undiagnosed adenocarcinoma of colon; also congenital neutropenia or prior radiation to abdomen. Treatment: Penicillin 3-4 million U IV q4h + Clindamycin 600-900mg IV q8h (alternatives imipenem, meropenem or vancomycin). Other interventions: debridement/surgical intervention, hyperbaric oxygen as adjuvant.

questions.question:
Q35 (2006 AM)
Clostridium sordelii infection post-partum/abortion

parts.text: A) 4 (or 6) clinical and lab features

cohort_answer.text: Clinical: women after gyne procedures (abortion, delivery, trauma); minimal to no pain, no fever or rash; n/v/abd pain; progressive refractory hypotension. Lab: GPB anaerobe; motile, spore forming; lethal toxin and hemorrhagic toxin; marked neutrophilia and high Hct

parts.text: 4 (or 6) clinical and lab features

cohort_answer.text: C. sordellii found in soil, sewage, human GI tracts, and vaginal flora following abortion. Anaerobic, spore-forming, Gram-positive bacilli. Many strains non-pathogenic, but some produce virulent toxins that can be fatal. Produces lethal toxin (LT) and hemorrhagic toxin (HT), causing widespread edema, necrosis and shock. Both LT and HT have antigenic similarity to C. difficile toxin A and B. C. sordellii neuraminidase (NanS) prevents leukocyte margination, leading to high neutrophilia. Generally susceptible to beta-lactams, clindamycin, tetracyclines and chloramphenicol. Presents clinically with rapid deterioration after abortion, postpartum, or gynecological procedure. Absence of fever is common. Absence of gas in tissues is common (consider C. perfringens or Bacteroides sp. if gas present).

questions.question: Patient with bloody bowel movements, develops spontaneous necrotizing cellulitis. Gram stain given, shows gram positive rods with absence of inflammatory response.

parts.text: Most likely organism?
What are two characteristic features seen on gram stain illustrated?
What is one condition directly associated with the acquisition of this infection?

cohort_answer.text: Clostridium septicum (spontaneous; C. perfringens more associated with preceding trauma; C. septicum predominant in neutropenia or GI malignancy via hematogenous spread, more aerotolerant). Gram stain: large gram positive/variable bacilli, often pleomorphic in clusters/chains, spores with terminal spore resembling a drumstick. Associated condition: GI malignancy (colon adenocarcinoma)

parts.text: Butcher cutting meat with a cellulitis progressing with cephalexin (GPB non haemolytic, vanco resistant)
Bullous lesions hemorrhagic with GPB
AML with line and bullous skin lesions with GPB

cohort_answer.text: A) Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae (pleomorphic nonsporulating GPB, can be alpha-hemolytic, vanco resistant intrinsically; transmitted handling saltwater fish/poultry/meat; tx penicillin or FQ x7-10 days). B) Clostridium perfringens (if traumatic) or Clostridium septicum (if spontaneous). C) Clostridium perfringens (traumatic) or Clostridium septicum (spontaneous); Bacillus cereus (rare in immunocompromised)

questions.question: What is the most likely bug in the following scenarios?

parts.text: Dog bite -> sepsis
Scalp wound cellulitis from fresh water
CVID with bloating and diarrhea
CA patient with bullous skin lesions and Gram stain showing GPBs

cohort_answer.text: 1) Capnocytophaga canimorsus. 2) Aeromonas. Others: Burkholderia, Edwardsiella, Plesiomonas, Pseudomonas. Salt water: Vibrio, Shewanella, Erysipelothrix. 3) Giardia. 4) Clostridium septicum (w/o trauma), due to the malignancy

questions.question: PM 14. What is the most likely organism to the species level in the following situations? AML with CVC and hemorrhagic bullae with GPB? (1); Fresh water exposure and necrotizing scalp cellulitis (1); CVID on interferon gamma with bloating and diarrhea (1); Post splenectomy patient who gets sepsis following a dog bite (1)

parts.text: AML with CVC and hemorrhagic bullae with GPB?
Fresh water exposure and necrotizing scalp cellulitis
CVID on interferon gamma with bloating and diarrhea
Post splenectomy patient who gets sepsis following a dog bite

cohort_answer.text: Clostridium septicum (in immunocompromised can cause gas gangrene without trauma, differentiating from C. perfringens; translocates from GI to hematogenous spread to skin; associated with colorectal CA). Aeromonas hydrophila (fresh water). Giardia lamblia/duodenalis. Capnocytophaga canimorsus.

questions.question: Name the bug: AML - fever hypotensive bullae on legs and GPB and gram stain; CVID with diarrhea and bloating; Asplenia patient with fever and hypotension

parts.text: AML - fever hypotensive bullae on legs and GPB and gram stain
CVID with diarrhea and bloating
Asplenia patient with fever and hypotension

cohort_answer.text: AML case: Clostridium septicum. CVID: Giardia lamblia. Asplenic: Pneumococcal sepsis; Meningococcal sepsis; Salmonella; Capnocytophaga; H. influenzae. Freshwater swimmer: Aeromonas spp.
